subject: Azura: runtime guardrail exception for p95 and standby nodes
messages:
From: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@azura.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@azura.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: runtime guardrail exception (p95 95ms / 99.99% uptime)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked promising. To move forward with a signed PO our engineering and compliance teams need two specific commitments:

- p95 inference latency <= 95ms for text-generation (avg seq 64 tokens)
- 99.99% uptime for our primary region, with standby nodes in us-west for failover

I realize these are tighter than Redwood's standard publicly documented SLOs. Azura is a strategic customer for us (pilot + integration into their triage workflow). Can your team outline what an exception path looks like, operational asks from Azura (e.g., can they limit burst concurrency, use smaller context windows), and what extra cost / reserved capacity this implies?

Attaching a short SLA template and our internal operational matrix. Procurement will start contract language once we have a service-level statement to review.

Appreciate a quick internal alignment — can we get an internal go/no-go today so I can update Ana's procurement timeline?

Best,
Ana
Ana Gomez
Head of Integrations, Azura Health
Attachments: azura_sla_request_20280427.pdf, azura_operational_matrix.xlsx

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: runtime guardrail exception (p95 95ms / 99.99% uptime)

Irene / team — quick feasibility note from engineering:

- p95 <= 95ms: Possible but only under these constraints:
  * Model family = distilled LLM-XX (quantized int8 recommended) or smaller 7B variant; larger 13B/70B models will not hit 95ms p95 at the requested seq length without dedicated NVLink pooling and nonstandard kernels.
  * Reserved dedicated pool (minimum 4x A100s equivalent) pinned to Azura, with continuous warm KV cache for session affinity.
  * Disable queuing retries and keep batch size <= 2 to preserve tail latency; this will reduce throughput.

- 99.99% uptime: Operationally demanding. To approach this we need:
  * Active-active across two availability zones in region (active traffic split) + cross-zone cold-standby to cover AZ blowups.
  * Proactive capacity burn tests, SLA runbook, and an agreed maintenance window policy.
  * SRE on-call escalation (L1 + L2) with 15-minute target response and warm standby engineers for P0s.

Cost impact (very rough): +55–80% on top of standard dedicated pricing for the reserved pool + premium SRE rotation (est. $25–40k/mo). Precise numbers after capacity planning.

Risks / product asks for Azura:
- Allow us to use the 7B distilled variant or accept a deliberate model variant fallback clause for heavy burst days.
- Agree to traffic shaping to limit sustained peak concurrency above agreed commit.

I can run a quick capacity test tomorrow if we get an approved model variant and a confirmed peak QPS target.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: runtime guardrail exception (p95 95ms / 99.99% uptime)

Irene / team — ops + CS notes to include in the internal SLO exception packet for procurement: 

1) Operational commitments we need from Azura:
   - Provide expected traffic profile (per-minute QPS distribution) and top 10 busiest user journeys (we will build cache warming rules).
   - Allow us to instrument a short redirect/proxy to maintain session affinity for KV caching.
   - Agree to an emergency maintenance contact and runbook sign-off.

2) Runbook / on-call impact:
   - 24/7 SRE rotation (two engineers on rotation); runbook to be jointly tested once per quarter.
   - P0 playbook: 15 min ack, 60 min mitigation objective.

3) Legal / procurement asks to include in SOW:
   - Fallback clause: if we cannot maintain p95 for two consecutive weeks despite mitigations, Redwood will be permitted to degrade to the next-approved model variant for up to 48 hours while remediations occur.
   - Scheduled maintenance windows: 3x/year, with 72h advance notice for non-emergent work.

Attachments: I pushed a starter SLO packet to the Drive link (https://drive.redwood/azura/sla-draft-v2). I recommend we propose a commercial uplift of 60% over baseline dedicated pricing and call out the model-variant clause.

Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ops-oncall-impact.pdf
